title: State Management Core Check
description: Check your understanding of local, global, server, and URL state plus common React state management tools.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which are common kinds of state in React apps? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: React apps often manage local, shared client, server, and URL-derived state.

questions.prompt: Where should simple state used by one component usually live?
questions.explanation: Keep state close to where it is used until sharing requirements justify moving it.

options.text: Data owned by a server and cached or synchronized in the UI

questions.explanation: Server state has remote ownership, loading, errors, caching, and revalidation concerns.

questions.prompt: What is URL state good for?

options.text: Shareable navigation state such as filters, search terms, and selected tabs

questions.explanation: URL state is useful for bookmarkable, shareable view state, not secrets or hidden mutable values.

options.text: Application state updates through actions, reducers, and a store

questions.explanation: Redux models updates with dispatched actions processed by pure reducers in a store.

options.text: Opinionated helpers such as configureStore and createSlice

questions.explanation: Redux Toolkit is the recommended way to write Redux with less boilerplate.

options.text: A small external store API with simple hooks

questions.explanation: Zustand offers lightweight external stores that React components can read with hooks.

questions.prompt: Context is good for passing values through the tree, but it is not a full server-state caching solution by itself.
questions.explanation: Context shares values; server state often needs fetching, caching, invalidation, and background revalidation tools.
